name: Garrison Reach
specific_features: Sunken metallic structures of artificial origin on the ocean floor
description: Garrison Reach is an ocean world of staggering depth, its surface broken only by scattered archipelagos of tidal plateaus that rise like watchtowers above endless blue-green seas. Submerged volcanic ranges form the planet's spine, their peaks colonized by coral formations of extraordinary density and complexity. The deepest trenches plunge beyond fourteen kilometers, where bioluminescent fauna drift through eternal darkness.

The air is thick with salt and moisture, and weather systems build with dramatic speed across the open ocean, delivering monsoon-force rains that batter the exposed plateaus. Between storms, the seas achieve an almost crystalline calm, their surfaces reflecting the pale binary stars overhead in sheets of molten light. The rhythm of Garrison Reach is tidal -- everything moves to the pulse of its three moons.

The archipelago plateaus show evidence of deliberate shaping, their edges too regular, their surfaces too level to be purely natural. More compelling are the sunken metallic structures found along the deepest trench walls -- enormous rectilinear forms encrusted with millennia of marine growth. Whatever built them is long gone, but the structures still emit faint electromagnetic pulses detectable by deep-sea probes.

The planet's rich marine biomass and unique coral-derived compounds have attracted pharmaceutical and biotech interests, though permanent settlement remains challenging given the limited dry land. Competing survey teams have established floating research stations above the sunken structures, racing to map and interpret what may be the remnants of an aquatic civilization. Garrison Reach guards its secrets beneath kilometers of dark water.
